newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia loses 1,000 kgs gold a year in smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia loses 1,000 kgs gold a year in smuggling.

text.p: At least 1,000 kg of Ethiopian gold is smuggled out of the country each year, officials said on Friday.
Ethiopian Gold Development Enterprise General Manager Tibebe Tafesse told Reuters the smuggled gold was produced by artisan miners based in southern Ethiopia and went to neighbouring countries.

Tibebe said that 50,000 residents of Ado Shakisso district in the south were considered artisanal miners. He said it had proved virtually impossible to control illegal mining in the area that covers some 1,300 square km of gold-bearing land.

He said the Enterprise had set up 14 gold centres for buying gold from artisanal miners but suggested that the best way to curb smuggling was to organise the miners into a small-scale enterprise (company).

"If the artisan miners were to be organised into cooperatives and helped to streamline their income, the vast amount of money which is lost could be channeled into the naitons' formal economy," Tibebe told Reuters.

Tibebe declined to name neighbouring countries that received the smuggled Ethiopian gold. But other mining sources said that businessmen from Kenya, which borders Ethiopia along the gold-bearing region of Borena, were the main culprits.
Tibebe also accused hundreds of gold shops mushrooming in Addis Ababa and all over the country of buying gold smuggled from the south of the Horn of African country.
Artisanal mining in Ethiopia dates back centuries.
The government says there are up to 500 tonnes of proven gold deposits in sites around Ethiopia.

Ethiopia's only operating gold mine at Lege Dembi, 300 km (190 miles) south of Addis Ababa, produces slightly below three tonnes of gold a year and published government estimates of its proven deposits range from 60 to 200 tonnes.
